source_refs.note: Published v2 baseline, 22 kb_candidates (KB-001..KB-022), feature FEAT-07-storefront-buyer-facing, 3 existing conflicts (CONFLICT-001/002/003) UNRESOLVED. Read-only reference, NOT modified by this artifact.

observations: All 3 upstream artifacts carry gate.decision = CONDITIONAL_PASS (none FAIL) -- all usable per process step 1. Their individual conditions (do not upgrade INFERRED->CONFIRMED_EXPECTED, do not resolve CONFLICT-PORTAL-001/MISMATCH-002, do not silently overwrite FEAT-07 store1=v1 claim) are honored below: nothing here is CONFIRMED_EXPECTED, and CONFLICT-PORTAL-001 is carried forward with all 3 sides intact, UNRESOLVED.

Object decision (per orchestrator, already made, not re-litigated here): this candidate targets OBJECT-ID OBJ-SDK (existing object, currently published version 2 with 22 kb_candidates and feature FEAT-07-storefront-buyer-facing). This artifact is a candidate for object version 3 (INCREMENTAL_UPDATE), ADDING new candidates KB-023..KB-044 only. KB-001..KB-022 already published in knowledge/products/teeinblue/objects/sdk/kb.json are UNCHANGED and NOT re-listed here.

New feature FEAT-08-product-page-settings-config introduced (portal surface, config page /product-page-settings) alongside the existing FEAT-07-storefront-buyer-facing (storefront surface). Both features live under the same object OBJ-SDK per orchestrator's convention that 'SDK' = the full storefront/customer-facing rendering surface, and this portal page directly controls that rendering.

MAJOR FINDING carried through verbatim (current_behavior_only, NOT normalized into a stronger claim): across all 67 portal controls observed on /product-page-settings (both tabs), and across the full storefront DOM for campaign 2595, store1 (instance 609, linh-explorer.myshopify.com) and store2 (instance 613, linh-explorer-2.myshopify.com) are IDENTICAL in this run's evidence. This directly contradicts the task's original premise (that config would differ by SDK v1/v2 per store) -- reported as observed fact, not resolved or explained further. See KB-025..KB-036 (portal) and KB-040..KB-042 (storefront).

CONFLICT-PORTAL-001 is the single most important conflict in this candidate: it now has THREE evidence sides (old KB claim store1=v1, new portal API sdk_version=2 for both, new storefront runtime re-check showing store1 now serves v2 markers too) and directly implicates the currency of KB-004/KB-005/KB-007/KB-010/KB-011 in the ALREADY-PUBLISHED object sdk v2. Per explicit instruction, this normalizer does NOT resolve it, does NOT mark those published items stale, and does NOT silently pick a side -- see conflicts[].

MISMATCH-001 (api-explorer) is carried forward as its own conflict entry (config_registry.instance.config schema declares ~38 keys, actual instance.config on /api/instances shows ~27 keys, only 1 name overlap) -- see conflicts[]. MISMATCH-002 is the same underlying fact as CONFLICT-PORTAL-001's evidence_b/evidence_c and is NOT duplicated as a separate conflict; it is referenced from CONFLICT-PORTAL-001 directly.

CONFLICT-001 (store1 ATC completion), CONFLICT-002 (dog/cat label mismatch) and CONFLICT-003 (store2 ATC first-attempt timing) already exist UNRESOLVED in the published knowledge/products/teeinblue/objects/sdk/kb.json. This run's storefront-explorer pass produced one new, symmetric, non-resolving data point relevant to CONFLICT-001's topic (KB-043) -- it is added as a NEW observation and explicitly does NOT close CONFLICT-001 (different scenario: an intentionally-invalid/incomplete personalization attempt, not the fully-filled-field scenario CONFLICT-001 is about). CONFLICT-002 and CONFLICT-003 receive no new evidence this run and are referenced unchanged.

The artwork-preview mechanism observed this run (img + 'tee-printarea' overlay div, zero [data-layer-id] SVG elements, identical on both stores) does not verbatim match either the pre-existing KB-010 description (store1/v1: static PhotoSwipe-style lightbox) or KB-011 description (store2/v2: live SVG with artwork-layer--layer-<n> ids). It is recorded as a new, separate observation (KB-042) and explicitly flagged in unknowns as unreconciled with KB-010/KB-011 -- not merged into either.

GET /api/instances?trashed (APIOP-001) binding to specific Elements & Behaviors / Styles & Colors form controls remains INFERRED (name/value correlation only, not a code-confirmed field-by-field contract) -- carried forward as INFERRED in KB-038, not upgraded.

Cross-layer mapping performed: portal ACT-IDs (ACT-01-01-001, ACT-01-04-001) linked to api-explorer's APIOP-001/APIOP-002 (same act_ids already present in action-api-map.json operations[].act_ids) and, where the underlying store/instance is the same, cross-referenced (not act_id-linked, since storefront-explorer uses its own SF-ACT-* namespace on a different page/object -- product page vs settings page) to storefront-explorer's SF-ACT-01/02/05/06 for instance 609/613 identity continuity. See cross_layer_evidence_map[].
assumptions: Inherited, not independently re-verified: portal-explorer's/api-explorer's assumption that GET /api/instances?trashed .config is what the Elements & Behaviors / Styles & Colors form renders from (name/value correlation only). Carried into KB-038 as INFERRED, not elevated.

This normalizer assumes 'FEAT-08-product-page-settings-config' as the feature slug for the new portal-config feature per the orchestrator's instruction to create a new FEAT-08 under OBJ-SDK; the exact slug wording is this agent's choice and may be adjusted by feature-profile-builder/reviewer.
unknowns: Whether sdk_version=2 for both instances (portal API, this run) and the matching storefront runtime markers reflect a genuine migration of store1 from SDK v1 to v2 sometime between 2026-09-12 and 2026-09-21, versus sdk_version being a config flag decoupled from the actual bundle served, versus the original FEAT-07 evidence being specific to a narrower condition not reproduced this run. Explicitly NOT decided here -- see CONFLICT-PORTAL-001.
Exact hex values behind ~13 color-picker fields on Styles & Colors (both stores) -- accessibility snapshot exposes them as swatch controls only (KB-035, KB-036).

Exact selected option for icon-only swatch controls: Font size, Toggle style, Alignment, Field's border radius (KB-034, KB-035) -- not distinguishable via accessibility tree, only screenshots capture visual state, not transcribed to a value in this run.

Content of sibling Store Settings pages (General Settings, Product Page Content, Customization Image, Shipping Methods, Inventory Locations, SKU Mapping) -- out of this run's object_target scope entirely, zero evidence.
Role/permission variance on /product-page-settings -- only 'owner' role tested this run (no TIB_USER_A_*/TIB_USER_B_* available).
Full write-path (Save/Reset) contract for /product-page-settings -- zero evidence in any of the 3 upstream artifacts, Save/Reset were never clicked (forbidden_actions).

Whether GET /api/settings' config_registry.instance.config (~38 schema keys) and GET /api/instances' .config (~27 actual keys, 1 overlap) describe the same namespace at different completeness, or genuinely different namespaces -- MISMATCH-001, unresolved.

Whether template option 3 (untested this run) reveals the same/different dependent-field set on either store; whether the img+tee-printarea preview mechanism (KB-042) and the select/text 2-level dependency shape (KB-041) generalize beyond campaign 2595/this template, or are specific to it -- flagged, not resolved.

Full add-to-cart completion (valid personalization through to a confirmed cart line item) was not achieved on either store this run -- CONFLICT-001 remains fully open; KB-043 is a different (invalid-state) scenario and does not address it.

sides.statement: config_registry.instance.config (from GET /api/settings) declares ~38 POSSIBLE instance-level config keys as a schema dictionary, including keys that read as plausible conceptual matches for observed Product Page Settings controls (e.g. show_cross_sell, group='Storefront SDK', plausibly matching OBS-024 'Show Cross-sell Personalization') -- but this is a documented/aspirational schema, not confirmed as what /product-page-settings actually reads/writes.
